question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{7x+2y}{x}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{7x+2(vx)}{x} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=7+2v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=7+v \\ \frac{1}{7+v}\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int\frac{1}{7+v}\,\mathrm{d}v&=\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \ln|v+7|&=\ln|x|+C_1 \\ |v+7|&=e^{C_1}|x| \\ v+7&=Cx \\ v&=Cx-7\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{x}&=Cx-7 \\ y&=Cx^2-7x\end{aligned}
$$

The signed constant $C$ absorbs $e^{C_1}$. Division by $v+7$ excluded $v=-7$; restoring it permits $C=0$, giving $y=-7x$.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{8x^3+y^3}{xy^2}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int v^2\,\mathrm{d}v&=8\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \frac{v^3}{3}&=8\ln|x|+C_1 \\ v^3&=24\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

Here $C=3C_1$ and the cube root is real. Restrict the solution to intervals where $y\ne0$.

\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{-7x+2(vx)}{x} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=-7+2v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=-7+v \\ \frac{1}{-7+v}\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int\frac{1}{-7+v}\,\mathrm{d}v&=\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \ln|v-7|&=\ln|x|+C_1 \\ |v-7|&=e^{C_1}|x| \\ v-7&=Cx \\ v&=Cx+7\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{x}&=Cx+7 \\ y&=Cx^2+7x\end{aligned}
$$

The signed constant $C$ absorbs $e^{C_1}$. Division by $v-7$ excluded $v=+7$; restoring it permits $C=0$, giving $y=+7x$.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$.

question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{x+y}{x}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{x+(vx)}{x} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=1+v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=1 \\ \frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{1}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int\mathrm{d}v&=\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ v&=\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{y}{x}&=\ln|x|+C \\ y&=x\ln|x|+Cx\end{aligned}
$$



The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$.

question.:question/problem:
Use the transformation $y=v(x)x$ to find the general solution of the following homogeneous differential equation.

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{-9x^3+y^3}{xy^2}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
With $y=v(x)x$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}&=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}(x) \\ &=x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{-9x^3+(vx)^3}{x(vx)^2} \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}+v&=\frac{-9+v^3}{v^2}=\frac{-9}{v^2}+v \\ x\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{-9}{v^2} \\ v^2\frac{\mathrm{d}v}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{-9}{x}\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\int v^2\,\mathrm{d}v&=-9\int\frac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ \frac{v^3}{3}&=-9\ln|x|+C_1 \\ v^3&=-27\ln|x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

From the transformation $y=vx$, we get

$$
v=\frac{y}{x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our solution, we finally obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^3&=-27\ln|x|+C \\ y^3&=x^3(-27\ln|x|+C) \\ y&=x\sqrt[3]{-27\ln|x|+C}\end{aligned}
$$

Here $C=3C_1$ and the cube root is real. Restrict the solution to intervals where $y\ne0$.

The solution is used on intervals where $x\ne0$ and $y\ne0$.
